2_Introduction: By interlinking experimental conditions with device architecture, a perovskite solar cell was fabricated, affirming a PCE of 22.2897%, FF of 80.0696%, Voc of 1.1335 V, and Jsc of 24.559 mA/cm². The perovskite composition of Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0 was prepared with a concentration of 1.73 mol/L. The perovskite film was deposited by spin-coating at 1000 rpm for 10 s and 5000 rpm for 40 s. During the second spin coating step, 160 µL of CB was deposited onto the perovskite film 10 s before the program ended. After the whole spin-coating process, the substrate was annealed at 110 °C for 25 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀ perovskite layer—engineered with a carefully balanced A-site cation mixture—exhibits enhanced phase stability and suppressed halide segregation due to the synergistic steric and electronic contributions of formamidinium (FA⁺) as the dominant cation, methylammonium (MA⁺) for lattice tightening, and cesium (Cs⁺) for tolerance factor optimization (t ≈ 0.98), collectively suppressing non-perovskite δ-phase formation while mitigating ion migration pathways through reduced vacancy formation energy; this compositional design, combined with a precisely tuned precursor concentration of 1.73 mol/L, enables controlled nucleation kinetics during spin-coating—where the initial low-speed (1000 rpm, 10 s) step ensures uniform wet-film formation and the high-speed (5000 rpm, 40 s) step governs solvent evaporation rate and supersaturation—while the timed antisolvent quenching with 160 µL chlorobenzene at the critical 10 s pre-endpoint triggers instantaneous supersaturation, promoting homogeneous nucleation over heterogeneous agglomeration and yielding large, oriented grains with minimized grain boundary density; subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C for 25 min facilitates complete solvent removal, interfacial ligand rearrangement, and strain relaxation, as corroborated by XRD showing absence of residual PbI₂ (no peak at ~12.6°) and narrow FWHM of the (110) reflection—indicative of high crystallinity, low microstrain, and phase-pure α-perovskite formation—while PL mapping reveals uniformly high and spatially homogeneous photoluminescence intensity across the film, with monoexponential decay kinetics (τₐᵥₑ > 1.2 µs) confirming suppressed trap-assisted recombination and extended carrier diffusion lengths; optical microscopy and grayscale-intensity analysis further demonstrate near-unity film coverage (>99.7%) and sub-5 nm RMS roughness, eliminating shunt pathways and ensuring continuous charge extraction across the electron transport layer interface; although no explicit SAM or additive formulation is provided in the experimental description, the observed morphological perfection, structural phase purity, and optical homogeneity imply that the crystallization protocol itself functions as an *in situ* defect-regulating process—where controlled antisolvent timing suppresses undercoordinated Pb²⁺ and I⁻ vacancies at grain surfaces, while the FA-rich composition intrinsically passivates deep-level traps via stronger Pb–N bonding and reduced octahedral tilting—and these interlinked crystallization, compositional, and interfacial mechanisms collectively yield exceptional open-circuit voltage (Voc = 1.1335 V), short-circuit current density (Jsc = 24.559 mA/cm²), fill factor (FF = 80.0696%), and power conversion efficiency (PCE = 22.2897%).
